quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: A person is considered legally intoxicated at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent means a person is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while intoxicated.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Use only mirrors to see other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Not worry about other traffic.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, the motorcycle's stopping distance:

options.text: May be increased.
May be decreased.
Is not a concern.
Will be the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be increased.
questions.explanation: Extra weight increases stopping distance. Start braking earlier when carrying a load or passenger in the sidecar.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to prevent a friend from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with activities while they sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Ask other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, arrange alternate transportation, keep them occupied, find excuses to delay them leaving, and get other friends involved. Waiting 15 minutes does not eliminate alcohol from the body.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:

options.text: Accelerating.
Braking.
Swerving.
Turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking.
questions.explanation: Downshifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle down.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is located:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The shift lever is in front of the left footrest. Use your left foot to shift. Lift the lever to go up a gear. Press it down to go down a gear.

questions.question: At intersections, the most common cause of crashes between motorcycles and cars is:

options.text: Drivers failing to yield the right-of-way to riders.
Riders not seeing drivers enter from side streets.
Drivers tailgating riders.
Riders not yielding to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers failing to yield the right-of-way to riders.
questions.explanation: Over half of motorcycle-car crashes at intersections happen because drivers fail to yield to riders. Be extra alert at intersections.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Check your mirrors more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay away from parked cars to avoid hazards like opening doors or people stepping out. This gives you more space to react.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Allow one rider to fully pass before the next rider passes.
Allow several riders to pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal no other motorcycles are coming.
Pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow one rider to fully pass before the next rider passes.
questions.explanation: Each rider should complete their pass and return to the group formation before the next rider passes.

questions.question: After drinking, what reduces the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Exercise
Coffee
Time
Food

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing else speeds up this process.

questions.question: When braking normally, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Switch between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you avoid?

options.text: Reducing your speed.
Making sudden moves.
Using both brakes.
Braking quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking quickly.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if you need to brake.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: In pairs.
In a staggered line with several riders passing at once.
One rider at a time.
Without passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: One rider at a time.
questions.explanation: Group riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next rider starts.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Brake gradually.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make a wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean forward. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: Alcohol quickly enters the brain. What is affected first?

options.text: Judgment
Speech
Balance
Vision

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects judgment and decision-making before it affects other abilities, even before you reach the legal limit.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how is stopping affected?

options.text: Stopping is easier than riding without a sidecar.
Stopping takes longer than riding without a sidecar.
You cannot stop.
Stopping is about the same as riding without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping takes longer than riding without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which means you need more braking force to stop. Stopping takes longer when going downhill.

questions.question: What does an experienced rider do?

options.text: Changes position within the lane as conditions change.
Stays in one spot in the lane at all times.
Moves side to side in the lane to be more visible.
Travels only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes position within the lane as conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle rider can use three different lane positions. Choose the position that is safest based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
Stopping sooner than expected.
Popping a tire.
Taking too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Pressing the brakes too hard can cause you to lose grip and crash.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to change lane position as conditions change.
Travel faster than normal to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Follow the vehicle ahead very closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to change lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Stay flexible about your lane position at night. Use safe riding strategies in difficult conditions.

questions.question: When turning a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the grip toward the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip away from the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When moving faster than walking speed, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the grip toward the direction you want to turn to make the bike lean the right way.
